info.name: Tokri API
info.description:
# Tokri API

Multi-vendor grocery delivery. Every endpoint the service exposes, grouped
by **who is allowed to call it**.

## Start here

Open **00 · Sign in** and run the login for the role you want. Each one
saves its token into a collection variable, so the folders below work
immediately afterwards — no copying JWTs by hand.

## How authorisation works

The API is **deny by default**. A global guard chain runs on every request:

```
ThrottlerGuard -> JwtAuthGuard -> RolesGuard -> VendorScopeGuard -> ResourceOwnerGuard
```

A route is only reachable without a token if it is explicitly marked
`@Public()`, and there are 17 of those out of 175.

`VendorScopeGuard` is worth calling out: a vendor cannot reach another
vendor's data by changing an id in the URL. The scope comes from the token,
never from the request.

## Conventions

* **Money is always INTEGER PAISE.** ₹429 is `42900`.
* **Lists paginate** with `?page=&limit=` and answer
  `{ data, meta: { page, limit, total, pages } }`.
* **Errors are RFC 7807** problem documents, with a machine-readable
  `errors.code` where one exists.
* **Validation is strict.** An unknown query parameter or body field is a
  `400`, never a silent ignore.

item.name: 00 · Sign in
item.description: Run one of these first. Each saves its token into a collection variable that the matching role folder already references.

exec: // Saves the token so every super admin request below just works.

request.description:
Signs in and **saves the token** into `{{superAdminToken}}`.

Set `{{superAdminPassword}}` first — it ships EMPTY on purpose. The value is the matching `SEED_*_PASSWORD` in `apps/api/.env`, which is gitignored; this collection is not, so it does not carry the password.

`identifier` takes an email OR a 10-digit phone number.

Rate limited to `THROTTLE_AUTH_LIMIT` attempts per minute per IP — budget one login per role.

Verify the OTP and receive a short-lived registrationToken

**Auth** — none. This route is `@Public()`.

**Responses** — `200`

Liveness probe

Answers as long as the process is up. It touches nothing else on purpose: a liveness probe that checks the database restarts a healthy API every time the database hiccups.

**Auth** — none. This route is `@Public()`.

**Responses** — `200`

Readiness probe

Whether this instance can actually serve traffic: MongoDB reachable, and the deployment a REPLICA SET rather than a standalone mongod. Transactions do not exist on standalone, and without them the checkout stock reservation cannot be atomic — so a standalone deployment is not ready even though it answers.

**Auth** — none. This route is `@Public()`.

**Responses** — `200`

item.name: Resolve a serviceable PIN code to its approximate centre

request.description:
Resolve a serviceable PIN code to its approximate centre

The non-map way to get a delivery point. `CreateAddressDto` requires lat/lng, and the web app normally collects them from a map pin — which is unavailable wherever Google Maps is not billed. Reads the same static table as `?pincode=` on the two browse routes; never a paid geocoding call. An unserviceable PIN is a 400 carrying `PINCODE_NOT_SERVICEABLE` and the list that does work.

**Auth** — none. This route is `@Public()`.

**Responses** — `200`

item.name: Market-wide search and aisle browsing, across every store

query.description: Field name, optionally prefixed with `-` for descending.

Indian PIN code, consulted only when lat/lng are absent. Same static table as GET /stores; an unlisted PIN is a 400 carrying the serviceable list, not a silently unfiltered page.

request.description:
Market-wide search and aisle browsing, across every store

The store-scoped listing above is `GET /stores/:id/products`; this is its platform-wide sibling — every APPROVED, OPEN vendor's products, filtered by `q` (the `searchText` text index, never a regex scan) and/or `aisleKey`. Each row carries `store:{id,slug,storeName,distanceKm}`; `distanceKm` is null unless `lat`/`lng` or a serviceable `pincode` were supplied. Neither FILTERS here — they only measure. There is no `radius`; that belongs to `GET /stores`, where it actually narrows the list.

**Auth** — none. This route is `@Public()`.

**Responses** — `200`

request.description:
Serviceable stores, nearest first

With `lat`/`lng` the list is a $geoNear ranked by distance and filtered to stores whose own serviceRadiusKm actually covers the caller. Without them it is an ordinary list ranked by rating, and `distanceKm` is null.

**Auth** — none. This route is `@Public()`.

**Responses** — `200`

The store catalogue

Filters: `category` (id or slug), `aisleKey`, `q` (text index). Sorts: name, -name, price, -price, createdAt, -createdAt, relevance (requires `q`). Each row carries live `inStock` / `availableQty` read from the inventory collection.

**Auth** — none. This route is `@Public()`.

**Responses** — `200`

item.name: Razorpay payment webhook — the source of truth (§8.3)

request.description:
Razorpay payment webhook — the source of truth (§8.3)

HMAC-verified over the raw body. Always answers 200 for a validly-signed event (even one this platform ignores), because a non-2xx makes Razorpay retry forever; answers 401 only when the signature itself is missing or wrong.

**Auth** — none. This route is `@Public()`.

**Responses** — `200`, `401`

Delete an address

Deleting the default promotes the next most recent one.

**Auth** — bearer token, role must be `customer`.

**Responses** — `200`

One address

**Auth** — bearer token, role must be `customer`.

**Responses** — `200`, `404`

Save an address

The first address saved is always the default. Setting `isDefault` demotes the previous one, so there is exactly one.

**Auth** — bearer token, role must be `customer`.

**Responses** — `201`

The caller's addresses, default first

**Auth** — bearer token, role must be `customer`.

item.name: Add to the basket (increments an existing line)

request.description:
Add to the basket (increments an existing line)

If the active basket belongs to a DIFFERENT store it is PARKED, never destroyed (locked decision #1), and returned as `parked`. If this store had a parked basket, it is restored and added to.

**Auth** — bearer token, role must be `customer`.

**Responses** — `201`, `409`

Empty the active basket

**Auth** — bearer token, role must be `customer`.

**Responses** — `200`

Remove one line

**Auth** — bearer token, role must be `customer`.

**Responses** — `200`

item.name: Set a line to an absolute quantity

request.description:
Set a line to an absolute quantity

**Auth** — bearer token, role must be `customer`.

**Responses** — `200`, `404`

Set the active basket aside

Parked baskets are restorable for seven days (TTL) and are listed on every cart response as `parkedCarts`. Adding an item from that store restores it.

**Auth** — bearer token, role must be `customer`.

**Responses** — `200`, `409`

item.name: The current basket, re-validated against live data

query.description: Which store's cart to read. Omitted, the ACTIVE cart is returned.

request.description:
The current basket, re-validated against live data

Every line is compared to the live product and inventory. Per-line `flags` report `price_changed`, `out_of_stock`, `reduced_qty` and `unavailable`. Nothing is silently corrected: a stale cart is the single biggest cause of a failed checkout, and the customer has to be the one who decides what to do about it.

**Auth** — bearer token, role must be `customer`.

**Responses** — `200`

Place the order

Reserves stock atomically (§8.2), re-prices server-side, and creates the order as PLACED with a commission snapshot and a hashed delivery OTP — all in one transaction. The plaintext OTP is in the response EXACTLY ONCE and is never readable again.

**Auth** — bearer token, role must be `customer`.

**Responses** — `201`, `400`, `409`, `503`

item.name: Re-price and re-check the basket without placing anything

request.description:
Re-price and re-check the basket without placing anything

Returns the server-side total, the live per-line flags, whether the address is inside the store's delivery radius, whether COD is available at this amount, and an `issues[]` list. `checkoutReady` is true only when `issues` is empty.

**Auth** — bearer token, role must be `customer`.

**Responses** — `200`

Cancel an order

Free while the order is still PLACED — the reserved stock goes straight back on the shelf and any coupon use is released. Once the store has accepted it, 409 `CANCELLATION_NEEDS_APPROVAL` (locked decision #8).

**Auth** — bearer token, role must be `customer`.

**Responses** — `200`, `409`

One order in full

**Auth** — bearer token, role must be `customer`.

**Responses** — `200`, `404`

query.description: Field name, optionally prefixed with `-` for descending.

request.description:
The caller's orders, newest first

**Auth** — bearer token, role must be `customer`.

**Responses** — `200`

Where the order is

The rider position is reported exactly as last received, with `lastSeenAt` and `ageSeconds`. It is never interpolated or refreshed server-side. `eta.basis` says where the time came from.

**Auth** — bearer token, role must be `customer`.

**Responses** — `200`

Client-side payment confirmation (optimisation only)

Verifies the Razorpay checkout-sheet signature and applies the same transition the webhook would. A no-op if the webhook already landed. Never the authority — see §8.3.

**Auth** — bearer token, role must be `customer`.

**Responses** — `200`, `401`, `409`

request.description:

item.name: Activate, hold or suspend a rider

request.description:
Activate, hold or suspend a rider

The login account moves with the record, in one transaction, and a suspension revokes the refresh-token family. Refused with 409 while the rider is carrying an order.

**Auth** — bearer token, role must be `vendor`.

**Responses** — `200`, `403`, `404`, `409`

Onboard a rider

Creates the DELIVERY `User` and the `DeliveryPartner` record in ONE transaction. The password is hashed with argon2id + the environment pepper and is never echoed back or written to the audit trail.

**Auth** — bearer token, role must be `vendor`.

**Responses** — `201`, `403`, `404`, `409`

One rider

**Auth** — bearer token, role must be `vendor`.

**Responses** — `200`, `403`, `404`

item.name: Remove a rider who has no order history

request.description:
Remove a rider who has no order history

Deletes the partner record and its login account in one transaction. Refused with 409 once any order references them — deleting would orphan delivery history; suspend instead.

**Auth** — bearer token, role must be `vendor`.

**Responses** — `204`, `403`, `404`, `409`

request.description:
Adjust many products in ONE transaction

A stock-take. All lines land or none do — a partially applied batch leaves the vendor unable to tell which lines took effect.

**Responses** — `201`, `403`, `404`, `409`

item.name: Adjust stock by a signed delta

request.description:
Adjust stock by a signed delta

Stock is ADJUSTED, never SET — an `InventoryLog` row is written in the SAME transaction, so the log always reconstructs the current quantity. A decrement past zero is a 409: the `$gte` guard lives in the query filter, so check and write are atomic.

**Auth** — bearer token, role must be `vendor`.

**Responses** — `200`, `403`, `404`, `409`

**Auth** — bearer token, role must be `vendor`.

Stock board (paginated)

Ordered worst-first: out of stock, then deepest under threshold. Filters: `lowStock`, `outOfStock`, `categoryId`, `q` over name/sku/brand.

**Auth** — bearer token, role must be `vendor`.

**Responses** — `200`, `403`, `404`

query.description: Field name, optionally prefixed with `-` for descending.

request.description:
The per-product movement trail (paginated)

Every adjustment already writes an `InventoryLog` row in the same transaction as the stock change; this reads it back, newest first.

**Auth** — bearer token, role must be `vendor`.

**Responses** — `200`, `403`, `404`

Accept a PLACED order

`etaMinutes` is the promised prep time; it is recorded on the status-history row for the `order.accepted` event.

**Auth** — bearer token, role must be `vendor`.

**Responses** — `200`, `403`, `404`, `409`

item.name: Assign one of the store’s own riders

request.description:
Assign one of the store’s own riders

Order status, `deliveryPartnerId`, the rider’s `activeOrderId` and their availability all move in ONE transaction. A busy or suspended rider is a 409; another store’s rider is a 404.

**Auth** — bearer token, role must be `vendor`.

**Responses** — `201`, `403`, `404`, `409`

Decline an order

`reason` is REQUIRED. A rejection with no reason gives support nothing to say and the customer nothing to act on.

**Auth** — bearer token, role must be `vendor`.

**Responses** — `200`, `400`, `403`, `404`, `409`

Drive the order forward

PACKING, READY_FOR_PICKUP and CANCELLED (reason required). REJECTED and ASSIGNED have their own endpoints because they carry payload the state machine cannot express.

**Auth** — bearer token, role must be `vendor`.

**Responses** — `200`, `403`, `404`, `409`

Full order detail

Items, pricing, delivery address, status history, customer and rider. The delivery OTP hash is never serialised.

**Auth** — bearer token, role must be `vendor`.

**Responses** — `200`, `403`, `404`

item.name: Partial fulfilment — drop lines and auto-refund

request.description:
Partial fulfilment — drop lines and auto-refund

Locked decision #9. Send EVERY line’s desired state. Totals are recomputed server-side (discount and tax scale pro-rata, the delivery fee does not, and the commission percentage is the checkout snapshot) and the refund difference is written as a LedgerEntry in the same transaction. Allowed only while the order is ACCEPTED or PACKING.

**Auth** — bearer token, role must be `vendor`.

**Responses** — `200`, `400`, `403`, `404`, `409`

Create a product

Writes the product, its inventory row and the opening stock log in ONE transaction. `slug` and `searchText` are derived server-side.

**Auth** — bearer token, role must be `vendor`.

**Responses** — `201`, `403`, `404`, `409`

request.description:
Delete a product and its inventory row

**Responses** — `204`, `403`, `404`, `409`

item.name: Presigned S3 PUT for a product image

request.description:
Presigned S3 PUT for a product image

The file NEVER passes through this API. `contentType` is allowlisted and `sizeBytes` is capped at 5 MB — and both are SIGNED into the URL, so storage rejects anything else rather than trusting the browser. Returns 503 while object storage is unconfigured; the rest of the module keeps working.

**Auth** — bearer token, role must be `vendor`.

**Responses** — `201`, `403`, `404`, `503`

**Auth** — bearer token, role must be `delivery`.

**Responses** — `200`, `403`, `409`

item.name: One offer in full — the confirm screen

request.description:
One offer in full — the confirm screen

Everything the rider must see BEFORE the money moves: the item list, pickup and drop, the payout, their current balance, and the bounds the pick fee will be drawn from. The exact fee is drawn at accept time, so the range is the only statement that is true when it is made — and showing nothing would mean the rider discovers the charge after it has been taken.

item.name: Take the job — and pay the pick fee

request.description:

Moves the order READY_FOR_PICKUP → ASSIGNED, holds the rider and charges a RANDOM pick fee in [RIDER_PICK_FEE_MIN_PAISE, RIDER_PICK_FEE_MAX_PAISE], all in ONE transaction. Any competing offer on the same order is cancelled. Returns the active order plus `pickFeePaise` and the resulting `walletBalancePaise`, so the app can show the charge the instant it happens.

**Auth** — bearer token, role must be `delivery`.

**Responses** — `200`, `402`, `403`, `404`, `409`

ASSIGNED → PICKED_UP

The goods have left the store.

This is the initial paint; `delivery.location_updated` on the order room moves the marker afterwards, so the app never polls this in a loop.

**Auth** — bearer token, role must be `delivery`.

The code is compared against a stored hash in constant time. A wrong code is 400 with `attemptsRemaining`; the fifth wrong code LOCKS the delivery (423) and only an admin can complete it. The code is never logged or echoed back.

The file NEVER passes through this API. `contentType` is allowlisted and `sizeBytes` is capped at 5 MB — and both are SIGNED into the URL, exactly like the vendor product-image presign. Returns 503 while object storage is unconfigured; the rest of the module keeps working. Send the resulting `publicUrl` back as `photoUrl` on `POST .../deliver`.

The same three fields and the same HMAC path as `POST /payments/:orderId/verify`. The amount credited comes from the STORED attempt, never from the request body. Idempotent: a second call on a paid attempt moves no money and reports the same balance.

request.description:
Vendor list (paginated)

Filter by `status` and `q` (store name, slug, city, pincode). Each row carries lifetime `gmv` (INTEGER PAISE) and `orderCount`, joined from orders excluding cancelled and rejected. Sortable on createdAt, storeName, commissionPct, rating, status, gmv, orderCount.

**Auth** — bearer token, role must be `admin`.

**Responses** — `200`

Credit a rider wallet (SUPER_ADMIN)

How a rider actually gets money while there is no payment gateway. Written as an ADJUSTMENT with `createdBy` set — NOT as a TOPUP, which would corrupt `lifetimeToppedUpPaise`, a figure somebody will reconcile against gateway settlements. Audited, and the note is mandatory.

**Auth** — bearer token, role must be `super_admin`.

**Responses** — `201`, `404`

Update platform settings (SUPER_ADMIN only)

Merge semantics: an omitted key keeps its current value. Each key is upserted individually so two admins editing different fields do not clobber one another. Every change is audited with a diff of only the keys that moved.

**Auth** — bearer token, role must be `super_admin`.

**Responses** — `200`, `403`

item.name: Generate settlements for a period (SUPER_ADMIN only)

request.description:
Generate settlements for a period (SUPER_ADMIN only)

Rolls DELIVERED orders in the window into one Settlement per vendor and reconciles the LedgerEntry rows. Safe to run twice: { vendorId, periodStart, periodEnd } is unique, so a repeat run reports the vendor under `skipped` instead of paying the week out again.

**Auth** — bearer token, role must be `super_admin`.

**Responses** — `201`, `403`

Mark a settlement paid (SUPER_ADMIN only)

Requires an `Idempotency-Key` header: a retried request replays the original response rather than writing a second payout row. An already-paid settlement is a 409 regardless of the key.

**Auth** — bearer token, role must be `super_admin`.

**Responses** — `200`, `403`, `409`

Create an ADMIN

The role is fixed to ADMIN by the service and is not a field on the body. A SUPER_ADMIN can NEVER be created through the API — the only one is provisioned by the seed script from `.env`.

**Auth** — bearer token, role must be `super_admin`.

**Responses** — `201`, `409`

Delete a team member

Suspension is the normal action. Refused for your own account and for seeded system accounts, which are the break-glass identities.

**Auth** — bearer token, role must be `super_admin`.

**Responses** — `204`, `403`

**Auth** — bearer token, role must be `super_admin`.

Suspension is the normal operational action. Deletion exists for mistakenly-provisioned accounts and erasure requests.

**Auth** — bearer token, role must be `super_admin`.

Provision an account (SUPER_ADMIN only)

Requires an `Idempotency-Key` header: a retried request replays the original response instead of creating a second account. `status` is derived from `role` and can never be supplied by the caller; SUPER_ADMIN cannot be created here at all.

**Auth** — bearer token, role must be `super_admin`.

**Responses** — `201`, `403`, `409`
